messages:
support-ops: Customer reported 404s after updating to @redwood/sdk v0.22. Says `client.chat.create` now returns undefined route. Repro steps attached.
customer-ops: TL;DR: we upgraded our TS SDK from 0.20 -> 0.22 and started getting 404s for chat creation. No other changes. latency looks normal, just immediate 404.
jordan.dev: Can you paste exact request you're sending (code snippet) + the error body? Also which API host are you hitting (host header/region)?
support-ops: Here’s the snippet from customer, redacted keys:
```ts
import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.chat.create({
  model: 'redwood-medium',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello' }]
});
```
Error: 404 Not Found
Response body: { "error": "route_not_found", "route": "/v1/chat/create" }
maria.lead: Huh. In v0.20 SDK the client used `chat.create` which mapped to `/v1/chat/create`. In 0.22 we changed the generated method to `chat.createConversation` and the runtime expects `/v1/conversations.create` in some regions. Looks like their package method is calling old route mapping but server side already deprecated it -> mismatch.
sam.engineer: Can they confirm the package.json lockfile? I've seen yarn.lock still pin older helper code while node_modules has mixed files. Could be they installed 0.22 but a transitive module kept a shim.
support-ops: Customer says `npm ls @redwood/sdk` -> shows `@redwood/sdk@0.22.0` and also `@redwood/sdk-legacy-shim@0.19.3` (??). They said they pulled latest, rebuild, same issue.
maria.lead: Temporary workaround: call the HTTP endpoint directly with the expected param names. Example:
```js
// raw fetch to avoid SDK mapping
await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/conversations.create', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.RW_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-medium', input: [{ role: 'user', text: 'Hello' }] })
});
```
This bypasses SDK route mapping and should succeed.
jordan.dev: Thanks. We should check two things: 1) server routing fallback for old `/v1/chat/create`, 2) SDK publish made a breaking method rename without proper compatibility layer. I'll reproduce locally with a minimal install.
sam.engineer: Repro steps I used locally:
1) `npm i @redwood/sdk@0.22.0`
2) create file index.ts with the snippet above
3) `node -r ts-node/register index.ts`
Observed: client.chat.create throws 404 with route `/v1/chat/create` present in stack.
deploy-bot: Noted: routing rule for `/v1/chat/create` was removed in canary region on 2026-03-10 as part of conversations consolidation. That could explain sudden break for customers in that region. Rolling retention policy favored new `/v1/conversations.create` only.
maria.lead: Proposed fixes:
- Short term: add server-side redirect/fallback for `/v1/chat/create` -> `/v1/conversations.create` for 7 days.
- Medium: publish @redwood/sdk 0.22.1 that restores a compatibility method `chat.create` which calls `conversations.create` under the hood and logs deprecation.
- Notify customers and update changelog + migration guide.
support-ops: Customer accepted raw-HTTP workaround for now, but asked for ETA on proper SDK patch.
jordan.dev: I'll prepare PR to reintroduce compatibility shim + add unit test asserting route mapping. Target patch release 0.22.1 within 24 hours. I'll include a clear migration note.
sam.engineer: Also recommend we scan npm for `@redwood/sdk-legacy-shim` installs and DM owners; could be a transform plugin from older templates.
maria.lead: I'll open an incident ticket to add a fallback in the router for one week and coordinate the SDK patch + release comms. tagging @ops for the rollout window.
support-ops: Customer notified. Marking as high-priority P1 for SDK compatibility. :white_check_mark:
